request.instruction: make with one sub and two speaker

product.name: Portable 2.1 Bluetooth speaker (sample)
product.summary: Revised to a 2.1 layout: two 40 mm satellite drivers and one 52 mm subwoofer in the same two-piece ABS housing, with the rear passive radiator now working with the subwoofer. One main board carries a Bluetooth audio module, a stereo class-D amplifier for the satellites, a low-pass filter and mono class-D amplifier for the subwoofer, and a linear Li-ion charger fed from USB-C. A single 18650 cell supplies both amplifiers directly and the logic through a 3.3 V regulator. Scale is taken from the USB-C port (8.9 mm wide) and the 18650 cell (65 mm long).
product.powerInput: USB-C, 5 V up to 1 A (charge only)

parts.name: Front grille
parts.function: Protects the three drivers and lets sound through.
parts.evidence: Visible across the full front face.

parts.name: Front baffle
parts.function: Holds the two satellite drivers and the centre subwoofer and seals the front of the acoustic chamber.
parts.evidence: A parting line runs round the body about 22 mm behind the grille. The three driver cut-outs are a redesign for the 2.1 request.
parts.unknowns: Rib pattern and boss positions inside are not visible. The baffle needs a new tool insert with three openings (40, 52, 40 mm); check that 6 mm of web between openings is stiff enough.

parts.name: Rear housing
parts.function: Main chamber. Carries the board, the cell, the key board and the port cut-out.
parts.process: Injection moulding with side-action for the port opening
parts.evidence: Port cut-out and four screw recesses visible on the back.

parts.name: Passive radiator
parts.function: Unpowered diaphragm that now works with the subwoofer to extend bass from the small sealed volume.
parts.material: Rubber surround with a steel mass plate
parts.evidence: Oval diaphragm visible through the rear slots.
parts.unknowns: The mass plate may need retuning for the subwoofer. Measure the resonance with an impedance sweep.

parts.name: Satellite driver, left
parts.function: Mid and treble speaker, 40 mm, 4 Ω, 3 W nominal, driven above about 200 Hz.
parts.material: Paper cone, neodymium magnet, steel basket
parts.evidence: User asked for two speakers plus a sub. Reduced from 45 mm to 40 mm and moved outward to make room for the centre subwoofer.
parts.unknowns: Impedance not confirmed. Measure DC resistance across the terminals. A closed-back basket or rear cup is advisable so the subwoofer pressure does not modulate the cone.

parts.name: Satellite driver, right
parts.function: Mid and treble speaker, 40 mm, 4 Ω, 3 W nominal, driven above about 200 Hz.
parts.material: Paper cone, neodymium magnet, steel basket
parts.evidence: User asked for two speakers plus a sub. Reduced from 45 mm to 40 mm and moved outward to make room for the centre subwoofer.

parts.name: Subwoofer driver
parts.function: Long-throw bass driver, 52 mm (2 inch), 4 Ω, 5 W nominal, driven below about 200 Hz.
parts.material: Coated paper or PP cone, rubber surround, neodymium magnet, steel basket
parts.evidence: Added at the user's request for one sub. 52 mm is the largest round driver that fits between the satellites and above the main board in the 66 mm tall housing.
parts.unknowns: Final choice depends on excursion and resonance. Pick a driver whose free-air resonance is below about 120 Hz and check it clears the board by measurement.

parts.name: Main board
parts.function: Carries the radio, both amplifiers, the subwoofer filter, the charger and all connectors.
parts.material: FR-4, 1.6 mm, 2 layers, green solder mask, HASL finish
parts.process: Single-sided SMT reflow, then hand-soldered wires
parts.evidence: Board edge visible behind the USB-C opening.
parts.unknowns: Layer count assumed from product class.

parts.name: Bluetooth audio SoC module
parts.function: Bluetooth radio, audio decode, stereo DAC, key scanning and LED control.
parts.evidence: No marking visible. Typical for this price class.
parts.unknowns: Read the top marking to identify the chip.

parts.name: PCB trace antenna
parts.function: 2.4 GHz meandered inverted-F antenna with a copper keep-out beneath it.
parts.evidence: Typical for module-based designs.

parts.name: Crystal, 24 MHz
parts.function: Reference clock for the radio.
parts.evidence: Required by the radio. Frequency assumed.

parts.name: 3.3 V regulator
parts.function: Low-dropout regulator. Drops cell voltage to 3.3 V for the logic and the subwoofer filter.
parts.evidence: A 3.3 V rail is needed from a 3.0 to 4.2 V cell.

parts.name: Class-D stereo amplifier (satellites)
parts.function: Filterless bridge-tied-load amplifier for the two satellites, about 2 W per channel into 4 Ω from the cell.
parts.evidence: Two satellite drivers and a single-cell supply point to a 5 V-class BTL amplifier. Smaller input coupling capacitors high-pass the satellites at about 200 Hz.

parts.name: Output ferrite beads, satellites
parts.function: Damp switching edges on the four satellite speaker lines to limit radiated emissions.
parts.evidence: Common with filterless class-D outputs on short leads.

parts.name: Class-D mono amplifier (subwoofer)
parts.function: Filterless bridge-tied-load amplifier for the subwoofer, about 2.5 W into 4 Ω from the cell.
parts.evidence: Added for the subwoofer. The Bluetooth SoC has only a stereo DAC, so the third channel needs its own amplifier.
parts.unknowns: Output is limited by the 3.0 to 4.2 V cell. A 5 V boost stage would raise it to about 3 W but adds cost and battery drain.

parts.name: Output ferrite beads, subwoofer
parts.function: Damp switching edges on the two subwoofer lines.
parts.evidence: Same practice as the satellite outputs.

parts.name: Subwoofer filter op-amp
parts.function: Sums left and right and applies a second-order low-pass at about 200 Hz to feed the subwoofer amplifier.
parts.evidence: A mono bass signal has to be derived from the stereo DAC output. A single op-amp Sallen-Key stage is the usual low-cost way.
parts.unknowns: If the chosen SoC has DSP and a spare DAC channel, the filter can move into firmware and this part can be dropped.

parts.name: Subwoofer filter resistors and capacitors
parts.function: Summing resistors and the RC network that sets the 200 Hz corner and the subwoofer level.
parts.evidence: Needed around the filter op-amp.
parts.unknowns: Values to be tuned by listening and measurement with the final driver.

parts.name: Bulk capacitor, 470 µF
parts.function: Holds up the cell rail at the satellite amplifier during peaks.
parts.evidence: Typical next to a class-D amplifier on a single cell.

parts.name: Bulk capacitor, 470 µF (subwoofer)
parts.function: Holds up the cell rail at the subwoofer amplifier during bass peaks.
parts.evidence: Added with the subwoofer amplifier. Bass peaks draw the largest current pulses.

parts.name: Li-ion charger
parts.function: Linear constant-current, constant-voltage charger. 4.2 V, about 1 A set by one resistor.
parts.evidence: Single cell charged from a 5 V port.
parts.unknowns: Charge current depends on the programming resistor value.

parts.name: CC pull-down resistors, 5.1 kΩ
parts.function: Identify the device as a power sink so a USB-C source enables 5 V.
parts.evidence: Required for any USB-C sink that charges from C-to-C cables.

parts.name: USB-C receptacle
parts.function: Charging input. Power-only variant.
parts.evidence: Port visible on the rear face.
parts.unknowns: Whether D+ and D− are routed is not visible.

parts.name: Status LED
parts.function: Shows pairing and charge state through a light pipe.
parts.evidence: Indicator window on the front edge.

parts.name: MEMS microphone
parts.function: Hands-free call microphone, bottom-port.
parts.evidence: Small port hole near the front edge.

parts.name: Key board connector
parts.function: Four-pin header for the key harness.
parts.evidence: Keys sit on a separate board on the top face.

parts.name: Li-ion cell, 18650
parts.function: Energy store. 3.7 V nominal, about 2000 mAh (7.4 Wh). Now supplies about 2 A at full-volume peaks.
parts.evidence: Product weight and run time are consistent with one 18650 cell.
parts.unknowns: Capacity on the label is often overstated. Measure with a discharge test. Run time will be shorter with the added subwoofer channel.

parts.name: Cell protection board
parts.function: Cuts the cell off on over-charge, over-discharge and short circuit.
parts.package: Small FR-4 strip under the sleeve
parts.evidence: Expected on any cell sold into a consumer product.
parts.unknowns: Some low-cost units omit it. Check under the sleeve at the negative end. Its over-current trip (typically about 3 A) must stay above the new 2 A peak draw.

parts.name: Key board
parts.function: Carries the three tactile switches under the top keypad.
parts.evidence: Three raised keys along the top face.

parts.name: Tactile switch
parts.function: Power and play, volume down, volume up.
parts.evidence: Three keys with a click feel.

parts.name: Silicone keypad
parts.function: Sealed key caps that press the switches through the top wall.
parts.evidence: Soft raised keys on the top face.

parts.name: Housing screw
parts.function: Clamp the rear housing to the baffle.
parts.evidence: Four recessed screw heads on the back.

connections.label: VBUS
connections.evidence: Charger input comes straight from the port.

connections.label: VBAT to satellite amplifier
connections.medium: Wire soldered to the B+ pad, then trace
connections.evidence: Peak at full volume: 2 × 2 W out at about 88 % efficiency. The B+ wire carries this plus the subwoofer and logic current, about 2.1 A in total.

connections.label: VBAT to subwoofer amplifier
connections.medium: Shared B+ wire, then a separate wide trace
connections.evidence: Peak at full volume: 2.5 W out at about 88 % efficiency.

connections.label: 3V3 to filter
connections.evidence: Quiescent current of a small CMOS op-amp. A clean regulated rail keeps amplifier noise out of the filter.

connections.label: Speaker out, left
connections.evidence: RMS values at 2 W into 4 Ω, about the limit from a single cell.

connections.label: Speaker out, right
connections.evidence: RMS values at 2 W into 4 Ω.

connections.label: Speaker out, subwoofer
connections.evidence: RMS values at 2.5 W into 4 Ω, reached with about 10 % distortion on a full cell.

connections.label: Audio, left and right
connections.protocol: Analogue line level, AC coupled, high-passed at about 200 Hz

connections.label: Subwoofer audio, mono
connections.protocol: Analogue, low-passed at about 200 Hz, AC coupled

controls.label: Power
controls.action: Hold to switch the speaker on or off.

controls.label: Volume down
controls.action: Lowers the volume of the satellites and the subwoofer one step.

controls.label: Volume up
controls.action: Raises the volume of the satellites and the subwoofer one step.

unknowns: The 2.1 layout is a redesign, not something seen in the sample: the subwoofer, its amplifier, the filter and the smaller satellites are all proposed parts.
Whether a 52 mm subwoofer and two 40 mm satellites really fit the existing 150 mm baffle. The model leaves about 6 mm between openings and 0.2 mm between the subwoofer basket and the main board.
Whether the satellites need sealed rear cups to isolate them from the subwoofer chamber pressure.
Exact Bluetooth chip. No marking is visible from outside. If it has DSP and a third output, the analogue bass filter can be removed.
Whether the amplifiers run from the cell directly or from a 5 V boost stage. Power figures here assume direct cell supply.
Whether the cell protection board tolerates the new peak draw of about 2.1 A.
Real cell capacity and the resulting run time with three channels.
Board layer count and whether the USB data lines are routed.
verifySteps: Remove the four rear screws, measure the inside of the baffle and confirm the 40 / 52 / 40 mm driver openings and the 26 mm subwoofer depth clear the board and the cell.
Photograph both sides of the main board and confirm there is free area near the centre for U4, U6, C2 and the filter parts.
Read the markings on U1, U2 and U3 under magnification and check whether U1 offers a spare DAC channel or DSP crossover.
Measure VBAT at the amplifier supply pins while playing bass at full volume. A sag below about 3.3 V or a protection trip means the cell or wiring is undersized.
Run an impedance sweep of the subwoofer in the closed housing to find the radiator tuning and set the crossover corner.
Measure the charger programming resistor to find the charge current.
Put a USB power meter in line to confirm input current while charging.
safety: Li-ion cell inside. Do not pierce, short or heat it. Disconnect it before soldering.
Peak cell current rises to about 2 A with the subwoofer. Use 22 AWG or heavier battery leads and confirm the protection board is fitted.
Discharge both bulk capacitors before probing near the amplifiers.
